messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 429 rate detected on /v1/generate (region: us-west-2). Error spike started ~T-2m. Autoscaler not adding capacity. Paging: @Samira @Shane 

Samira: I'm on it, looking at autoscaler and rate-limiter dashboards now.

Shane: I have console access and will tail the autoscaler logs, joining now.

Maria: CS says a handful of customers reported failures and timeouts — flagged customers A123, B456.

Samira: Quick findings: queue length jumped from ~20 -> 1200 concurrent requests. Token-bucket rejects spiked in same window. Looks like token_bucket burst dropped to 0 for "production" tier after the last policy rollout. That prevents burst smoothing during handoff -> immediate 429s.

Shane: Confirmed in logs: token_bucket::deny_count spikes align with 429s. Also note autoscaler reached max_pools for this pool and didn't scale further; so both capacity and throttling hit.

Samira: Posting diff from recently applied config (suspect PR #5423):
```diff
- tier: production
- token_bucket: { rate: 200, burst: 500 }
+ tier: production
+ token_bucket: { rate: 200, burst: 0 }
```
This looks like an accidental zeroing of burst value.

Shane: That PR was merged by deploy-bot as part of a policy cleanup. deploy-bot, can you revert?

deploy-bot: Reverting PR #5423 to rollback_tokenbucket_burst. Starting deploy to conf-stage -> conf-prod. ETA ~45s.

Samira: While rollback is in flight, we should do hot mitigations:
1) Temporarily set production tier burst to 1000 so existing queued users can drain.
2) Increase autoscaler max_pools from 10 -> 20 for 10 minutes to allow scale up.
3) Spin up warm pool nodes and route new traffic there.
4) Notify affected customers.

Shane: Executing 1 & 2 now.

Shane: Commands I ran:
```
# temp increase burst
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/configs/tokens -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -d '{"tier":"production","token_bucket":{"rate":200,"burst":1000}}'

# bump autoscaler max
rbacctl set autoscaler.max_pools 20 --duration=10m
```

deploy-bot: Rollback deployed to production (deploy id: deploy-2026-04-12-953). Config change applied by Shane also accepted. Warm pool provisioning started (3 nodes).

Samira: Monitoring: queue length peaked at 1.2k, now down to 140 and dropping. 429 rate reported: 18% -> 1.3% within 3 minutes post-mitigation. Good signal.

Maria: CS update sent to customers A123, B456, C789 with ETA and note that we mitigated. They reported partial recovery.

Ryan: We need follow-ups:
- Revert accidental policy change permanently and add PR guardrail to block burst=0 for prod tiers.
- Add unit/integration test in policy CI that rejects zero-burst merges.
- Postmortem with timeline + quantification of impact.

Samira: Agreed. I'll open the postmortem ticket and own remediation items. Quick notes for severity: Sev2, ~18 minutes of elevated 429s, affected subset of hosted API customers on prod tier. Impact: increased request failures and elevated latency for those customers.

Shane: Handoff: I'm taking the next 30m observation window. Current status: token bucket reverted, autoscaler max increased temporarily, warm pool active. Continue to watch error rate and scale events.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> RESOLVED. Summary: 429s returned to baseline after token_bucket rollback and temporary autoscaler limit bump. Postmortem required. Incident duration ~00:18:12.

Samira: Created ticket JIRA-9876: "prod token-bucket burst zeroed by policy rollout -> 429s during capacity saturation". Actions assigned: Samira (policy CI), Shane (autoscaler defaults review), Maria (customer comms draft).

Shane: Final note: we should add an automated canary that triggers synthetic traffic to exercise token-bucket burst behavior on policy changes. Prevents silent regressions.

Samira: Thanks all. Leaving detailed logs and graphs in the incident doc. Passing to on-call: @Shane now.

Maria: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
